Per-case descriptive features

Source: R/utils-scd-analysis.R
compute_case_features.Rd

Per-case descriptive features

Usage

compute_case_features(
  data,
  outcome_var = "outcome",
  phase_var = "phase",
  case_var = "case",
  time_var = "time",
  intervention_goal = c("increase", "decrease")
)

Arguments

data

Data frame containing SCD data.

outcome_var

Name of the outcome variable.

phase_var

Name of the phase variable.

case_var

Name of the case variable.

time_var

Name of the time variable.

intervention_goal

Direction of a desirable change: "increase" (default) or "decrease". For "decrease", NAP is reported as 1 - NAP and PND counts phase-B points below the phase-A minimum.

Value

A data frame of summary features with one row per tier (each combination of the grouping columns of tier_vars(), so a case identifier repeated across studies or a case measured on several behaviors gives separate rows), or NULL if requirements are not met. case holds the case identifier and tier the full tier label (e.g. "S1 / P1 / reading"). Within each tier, the _A features use the first run of a baseline-role phase (see phase_role()) and the _B features the next intervention-role run, so labels such as "Baseline 1" and later reversal phases do not change which phases are compared. The nonoverlap descriptives NAP and PND are computed in the direction given by intervention_goal.

Examples

d <- simulate_scd_data(n_cases = 2, n_phase_a = 6, n_phase_b = 6)
compute_case_features(d)
#>   case tier   mean_A   mean_B      sd_A      sd_B    slope_A     slope_B
#> 1   C1   C1 46.64336 48.05030  9.124774  6.483815  0.3550227 -0.09015397
#> 2   C2   C2 57.23262 48.13144 10.194156 11.155911 -3.4646165 -1.01825202
#>        cv_A      cv_B   autocor_A  autocor_B mean_diff pooled_SD       NAP
#> 1 0.1956286 0.1349381 -0.18254586  0.1115179  1.406941  7.915218 0.5833333
#> 2 0.1781179 0.2317801 -0.09699311 -0.1550718 -9.101179 10.685859 0.2222222
#>         PND phase_length_ratio trend_accel_A trend_accel_B
#> 1 0.1666667                  1     2.6576965     -13.22389
#> 2 0.0000000                  1     0.4468388     -13.09183
